text:
incident-bot: Alert: p99 streaming latency spike in eu-west-2 detected by SLO watcher (rolling 5m). p95 120ms -> 620ms, p99 280ms -> 5.2s, streaming stalls increased to ~28%. Auto-pager triggered. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/s/latency?range=5m :rotating_light:

maya_oncall: I'm on it. Paging oncall list. Noted customer-affecting streaming stalls. Starting triage.

eli_sre: Seeing a sharp increase in router tail across eu-west-2. Top symptoms: routing policy rollout 2026-03-12-rp-842 recently applied, weight rebalancer running. Hotshard signatures on shard 14/67 (heavy tokenized traffic).

kevin_router: Confirmed — router telemetry shows increased sticky-affinity collisions + weight oscillation for rp-842. Logs: ```[router] policy_apply id=rp-842 delta_weights={zone-a: +0.35, zone-b: -0.33} epoch=4829``` then a cascade of handoffs.

ara_prodeng: Any evidence of model/backpressure? Could also be request-size skew that breaks batching.

eli_sre: Checked model-side. No CPU/GPU saturation; infra looks fine. The hot signal originates at loadbalancer routing layer — many requests stuck in long tail waiting for KV cache warming, likely due to repeated misroutes between zones.

ops-bot: Runbook step 1: disable risky rollout. Command: ```rctrl rollout rollback --policy rp-842 --to=2026-03-08T12:00Z``` (requires oncall ack).

maya_oncall: ACK. Rolling back now. Running: ```rctrl rollout rollback --policy rp-842 --to=2026-03-08T12:00Z --confirm```

ops-bot: Rollback job started (job id rb-2026-4312). ETA ~45s.

kevin_router: While rollback proceeds, recommend temporary mitigation: disable cross-zone sticky-affinity for router pool euw2 to reduce hotkey stickiness. Command: ```routerctl set affinity euw2 cross_zone=false --temp 15m```

maya_oncall: Applied cross-zone sticky-affinity disable. Noted config id cfg-759.

chris_sre: I'm draining suspicious shard hosts in euw2 to break the hot-loop. `infractl drain --pool=router-euw2 --shard=14 --reason='hotloop mitigation'`

paul_network: Observed increased intra-zone latencies between zone-a and zone-b during spike: tcp_rtt 8ms -> 45ms for many connections, likely amplifying handoffs. Working on QoS policing to limit burst flows.

eli_sre: Rollback completed. Initial metrics: p95 620ms -> 240ms (improving), p99 5.2s -> 1.1s but still noisy. Streaming stalls down to ~12%.

maya_oncall: Good. Next: quarantine the hottest partition to avoid repeated warm-cache misses. Command: ```routerctl quarantine-shard --shard=14 --duration=30m --route=slow-fallback``` This will send new traffic to fallback pool with warmed caches.

kevin_router: Quarantine applied. Also enabling prefix-KV prewarm for quarantined shard: ```kv-prewarm start --shard=14 --buckets=1000```

ara_prodeng: Noting customer impact: two midsize customers reported intermittent streaming disconnects and degraded throughput. Sarah from support, can you confirm tickets and severity?

sarah_support: Yep — tickets #C-17821 and #C-17822, both on eu-west-2. Customers reported ~10-25% request failures and long waits. I've opened escalation notes and told customers we're actively mitigating; will follow up with timeline.

eli_sre: Monitoring dashboards show tail now stabilizing but there's residual p99 variance due to a small subset of long-running sessions. I recommend increasing fallback concurrency for streaming fallback path to absorb backpressure: `service-config set streaming.fallback_concurrency=64` temporarily.

maya_oncall: Done. Applied fallback concurrency=64 for euw2.

ops-bot: Post-mitigation checklist: 1) rollback complete, 2) cross-zone affinity disabled, 3) shard 14 quarantined + kv prewarm, 4) fallback concurrency increased. Continue monitoring for 30m.

paul_network: I've also applied rate-limit smoothing at the edge to cap burst fanout to internal routers (edge-rate-limit=120rps per-ip for a short window).

chris_sre: Observed success: p95 240ms -> 130ms over last 10m, p99 dropping toward 420ms. Streaming stalls under 5% now.

maya_oncall: Passing to next oncall for postmortem. @eli_sre please own the initial incident notes and postmortem draft. I'll file followups for customer comms.

eli_sre: Will do. Immediate action items I have: collect roll-forward diff of rp-842, capture RB timeline, collect router handoff traces (trace ids), and get full list of affected shards. Also toss in a small script to detect policy weight oscillation.

ara_prodeng: Add a mitigation proposal: require gradual weight step limit in rollout engine (max_delta_per_epoch=0.1) and circuit-breaker for rapid oscillations. That would prevent this class of misroute thrash.

maya_oncall: Noted. I'll open a ticket to product/rollout with priority P1 after the incident.

incident-bot: Incident resolved to mitigated state. Status: degraded -> operational. Duration: 42m. Pager closed.

eli_sre: Postmortem owners: eli_sre (lead), kevin_router (root cause), ara_prodeng (mitigation design), chris_sre (sigs/alerts). I'll post a draft in #postmortems within 24h.

sarah_support: I'll update affected customers with ETA and mitigation summary once the postmortem draft is available.

maya_oncall: Logging final notes and closing thread. If regressions appear, re-open page. :white_check_mark:
